html:
A Chinese admiral and court eunuch who led seven great fleets of the Ming dynasty across the Indian Ocean between 1405 and 1433. His ships reached Southeast Asia, India, the Persian Gulf, Arabia and East Africa.

He was born to a Muslim family in Yunnan. When Ming armies took Yunnan he was captured as a boy, castrated and placed in the household of the prince who later became the Yongle Emperor. He served him well in war and rose high.

The voyages were huge. The largest fleets carried over twenty thousand men on dozens of big treasure ships. They called at Malacca, Calicut, Hormuz and the coast of Somalia and Kenya, where the fleet visited Malindi. They traded silk and porcelain, brought rulers into the tribute system, and carried envoys and animals home, including a giraffe.

The voyages stopped after Yongle died. Officials thought them too costly, and the Ming turned to defending its northern border. Zheng He died during or soon after the last voyage. Decades later the Portuguese reached the same waters from the other direction.
